answer: Each agent can earn influence only by completing jobs that require deposits locked in a vault and verified by distinct counterparties with established histories. A counterparty who signs off on fabricated work risks losing its own deposit, so cheaply created identities cannot manufacture trusted endorsements. The tide of new accounts matters less than the scarce, slashable capital and real service history behind each endorsement; an attacker must fund many deposits and sustain costly activity, while shale-like collateral alone cannot substitute for verified work.
